reasons.A: Long cataloguing sentences with interpolated asides and semicolon runs, uncontracted period diction and 'I do not know that' hedging come closest to the passage's piling, genial movement.
reasons.C: Period register and cumulative avenue sentences fit well, and it ends with an exuberant turn, but the rhythm is more even and measured, and 'I don't know' breaks the author's uncontracted diction.
reasons.B: The period feel is right, but the staccato repetition ('stood still' x4, 'It was a great mess. It was a glorious mess.') and the anecdotal comic tone read as a different humorist, not this breathless catalogue.
reasons.D: Modern, explanatory register ('hold-up', 'self-importance', 'a bit of shared trouble') with tidy, reflective paragraphs and none of the passage's period exclamation or fragmentary sweep.
